about.text: Casein phosphopeptide–amorphous calcium phosphate: a material made from the milk protein casein that holds calcium and phosphate in a form the body can use. It is sold in products such as Tooth Mousse and MI Paste, under the Recaldent name, and deposits these minerals on tooth enamel to help repair early white-spot decay.

facts.v: Phosphorylated fragments of β-casein, αs1-casein and αs2-casein
Nanocomplexes of amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) held apart by the casein phosphopeptides (CPP)
Can take up fluoride, giving CPP-ACFP
